title: eo keys list --json — S3 key pairs
description: Emitted by `eo keys list --json` (src/eosdk/cli/commands/keys.py) as a JSON ARRAY, one element per key pair the credentials service reports for the account. Secrets are NEVER present here: the service reveals a secret exactly once, at creation, and only `eo keys create --export` prints it (SPEC §6.4). The projection is built by the command, not by a model, so this schema is the only description of it. Hand-written on purpose: it is a contract, not a projection. `additionalProperties` is true — downstream consumers must tolerate fields added later.

key.description: One key pair, as the credentials service lists it plus what eosdk knows locally.

access_key.description: Public identifier of the key pair; the argument `eo keys revoke` takes, and AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID for aws-cli/rclone interop.

organization.description: Owning organization as the service reports it; null when it reports none.

expiration_date.description: When the service will stop honouring this key, RFC 3339; null when the key does not expire.

label.description: Client-side label the key was created under. The credentials service has no label concept — the mapping lives in the local per-profile store (src/eosdk/auth/s3_keys.py), so a key created on another machine reads back as null even though it is the same key.

local_secret.description: Whether this machine holds the secret for this key. False means the pair is unusable for a transfer here (the secret is unrecoverable) and can only be revoked.
